expectation: a usage-place detector (exported names whose sibling names in the same module, sharing a name token, are all used by the same set of two or more other files; a sibling used by a strict subset of those files is flagged, naming the files missing it) points at where a recorded defect lives, at the commit that introduced it, better than chance and better than the October paradigm reading (x-b2a4fd77, component lift 1.32)

actions.text: corpus: every defect in the journal whose introduced commit resolves in git and whose files include a non-test .ts file (22 defects, 14 commits); the detector reads src and plugins .ts at a revision from git objects, consumers are other non-test files importing the name (static, type and destructured dynamic imports; re-exports followed), *.test.ts excluded as consumers, *.e2e.ts kept

D (detect, primary): at the introducing commit, the flags that commit created (present there, absent at its parent); hit when a new flag names a defect file (the flagged name's module or a missing-use file); baseline is the share of that tree's non-test .ts files the new flags name; lift = hit rate / mean baseline

F (foresee, head to head with x-b2a4fd77): at the parent of the introducing commit, every flag, scored at component level (a file's nearest folder with a spec, else its top folder under src) exactly as H1 was: lift = component hit rate / mean share of components flagged

N (noise): flags per tree on main today and new flags per introducing commit; and the detector run on main as of PR #188's head, as a sanity check that it names isLauncherHook and EARLIER_LAUNCHER (motivating case, not scored)

criteria.text: D: hit rate at least 20% and lift at least 3
F: component lift at least 2.0 (1.5 times the October reading's 1.32)
N: median new flags per introducing commit at most 5, and at most 40 flags on main today, so a reviewer could read them
the claim is dead if D and F both fail; with 22 defects from 14 commits a pass is directional, not proof

chose: judge paradigm detection by the complexity it lets the project remove, measured as counts that only go down (places a member is wired by hand, scattered branches on a set's values, duplicated patterns, undeclared sibling sets), not by whether it foresees defects
over: scoring detectors by lift against recorded defects, as x-b2a4fd77 and x-481e195d did
because: the owner's ruling: the goal is a project that gets simpler release over release, and a consolidation candidate is worth acting on whether or not a defect would have followed
human: we don't need to predict the future, we just need to steadily reduce the complexity of a project over time

expectation: deterministic candidate generators propose viable consolidations: run at the parent of a consolidation the project later made, some generator names the scattered sites it removed, better than chance; and on main today, most of a generator's top candidates are judged worth consolidating

actions.text: truth: 13 consolidation commits after the rebuild (ffce0b4a), labelled from commit text alone before any generator ran, frozen in scratchpad consolidation/truth.tsv (sha256 recorded in the first result); a consolidation's sites are the non-test .ts files under src and plugins it deleted lines from, files it created excluded

generators, each read from git objects at a revision: G1 usage groups (exported sibling names sharing a name word, used by the same two or more files; sites: the module and those files); G2 the mirror reading as it ships (query mirrors --rev, default filter); G3 scattered branches (a string-literal union or const list whose values are compared with === or case in three or more files; sites: those files and the definition); G4 written twice (a regex literal of 12 or more characters, or a string literal of 30 or more, in two or more files; sites: those files)

R recall: at each consolidation's parent, a generator hits when one candidate names at least two of its sites (one when it has one); chance per candidate is the hypergeometric probability that a random file set of the candidate's size names as many; lift = recall / mean chance recall; reported per generator and for the union

P viability: on main today, each generator's top 8 candidates by its own rank, pooled and shuffled with the generator hidden, judged by two blind subagents with one rubric (viable: folding them into one declared or derived source removes places kept by hand, is bounded work, and loses no meaning); a candidate is viable when both say so

criteria.text: R: the union hits at least half the consolidations with lift at least 2
P: at least one generator has at least half its top candidates judged viable by both judges

the claim is dead if the union hits under 30% or no generator reaches 30% viable; the mirror reading was built from several of these consolidations' defects, so its recall is tuned and is reported but not counted for R; judges stand in for the owner, whose rating would supersede theirs
